---
title: "Florida Bay Forward Drift"
subtitle: "Where does Everglades outflow go once it enters the Bay?"
---

## Overview

This project tracks simulated freshwater released at three Everglades outflow
points — **Shark River**, **McCormick Creek**, and **Trout Creek** — forward
through Florida Bay and the Florida Keys, for the two weeks following each of
8 historical water-quality sampling cruises. The goal is to see, for the
conditions actually present on each cruise date, which parts of the Bay and
Keys a given outflow event is likely to reach and how quickly.

## Model

- **Circulation model:** [SLIM4](https://git.immc.ucl.ac.be/slim/slim4) (UCL), 2D
  depth-averaged shallow-water equations, unstructured triangular mesh
  (~32,000 elements, 400 m near the coast grading to 6,000 m offshore),
  explicit Runge-Kutta time integration with wetting-and-drying enabled for
  Florida Bay's shallow flats.
- **Bathymetry:** NOAA BlueTopo survey data.
- **Tides:** FES2014 (8 major constituents: M2, S2, N2, K2, K1, O1, P1, Q1).
- **Open-boundary currents & sea surface height:** Copernicus Marine Service
  GLORYS12 reanalysis.
- **Wind:** ERA5 reanalysis, 10 m wind converted to surface stress via the
  Smith-Banke formula.
- **Particle tracking:** 200 particles per source (600 total), released at
  the start of each cruise's model window and tracked forward for its
  duration with a random-walk horizontal diffusivity ("Okubo" formula) layered
  on top of the resolved currents.

## Reading the animations

Each cruise page below shows the drift animation for that cruise's model
window. Positions are exported every 15 minutes for the first 6 hours after
release (when dispersion is fastest) and every 6 hours thereafter. Use the
play/pause button, the scrubber, or the left/right arrow keys to step through.
